title: Modern Physics: Quanta, Atoms, and Nuclei

questions.question: The energy of a single quantum of radiation of frequency ν is:
questions.rationale: Planck's relation E = hν assigns each quantum an energy proportional to frequency, with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

questions.question: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light of the same frequency:
options: Ejects more electrons at the same maximum kinetic energy
questions.rationale: Intensity sets the number of photons, hence the number of photoelectrons; the frequency alone fixes each electron's maximum kinetic energy.

questions.question: Light of photon energy 4.15 eV falls on a metal whose work function is 2.0 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is:
questions.rationale: Kmax = hν − φ = 4.15 − 2.0 = 2.15 eV — the surplus energy after freeing the electron from the metal.

questions.question: According to Bohr's model, an atom emits radiation only when:
options: An electron radiates while circling in a fixed orbit
An electron jumps from a higher to a lower energy level
questions.rationale: Electrons in stationary states do not radiate; light of frequency ν with hν = E₂ − E₁ appears only in a jump between levels.

questions.question: Isotopes are atoms that have:
options: The same mass number but different atomic numbers
The same atomic number but different mass numbers
Different numbers of protons and equal neutron counts
questions.rationale: Isotopes share the atomic number Z (same element) but differ in mass number A because of different neutron counts; equal-A pairs are isobars.

questions.question: When a nucleus emits an alpha particle, its mass number and atomic number become:
questions.rationale: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus carrying 2 protons and 2 neutrons, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2.

questions.question: A radioactive sample of 80 g has a half-life of 5 days. After 15 days the mass remaining is:
The Sun's energy is produced mainly by:
options: Fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium
questions.rationale: In the Sun's core, hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium at extreme temperature and pressure, converting a tiny mass defect into vast energy.

questions.question: Einstein's equation E = mc² expresses that:
options: Mass can be converted into energy and vice versa
questions.rationale: Mass–energy equivalence: a mass m disappearing (the mass defect) releases energy E = mc² with the huge factor c² ≈ 9 × 10¹⁶.

questions.question: De Broglie's matter-wave hypothesis gives a moving particle a wavelength of:
questions.rationale: λ = h/p links a particle's momentum p to its wave nature — the principle behind the electron microscope.
